what_happened: The operator stopped a job that kept failing. The trailer job (lineage 20261025-012657-hac3) was rejected three times and cost about $11. Each attempt passed its own checks but failed against a test history that had been built by hand. The operator split the work into two jobs. The first (20261025-031609-k0tt) builds a reusable realistic fixture. The second (20261025-031612-6239) makes the trailer change on top of it. The operator chose the split, and the job lineage was not the thing that failed.
cause: Each producer builds its own test history by hand, and nothing requires a shared fixture made through the real record and commit writers. A hand-built history can look right and still miss the shapes of real history. The check the producer runs and the check the verifier applies therefore use different inputs. Retries repeat the same fixture mistake, and Athena has no cap on retries, no check that a lineage keeps failing for the same reason, and no automatic step that splits the work. Only the operator's thrash-stop default ends the loop.
prevention: Provide one shared test fixture that builds repository history only through the real writers: job commits, records-only commits, and owner-path and intervention commits. Require any job that touches history, trailers or landing checks to test against it, and do not accept hand-built histories for those checks. Also add a retry limit: after two rejections of one lineage for the same kind of failure, Athena stops and proposes a split, for example fixture first and change second, instead of retrying.
proposed_request: Build a reusable test fixture that creates a realistic repository history by calling Athena's real writers. It must include job commits, records-only commits, owner-path commits and intervention commits, and branches in the shapes that occur in practice. Add tests showing that the fixture's output passes the existing history and landing checks. Document how later tests use it. Do not change trailer behavior in this job. Make the work reusable so the trailer change (20261025-031612-6239) and later history-related jobs can build on it.
